desc:
A string s is built from a unit u if s equals u written one or more times in a row. Every string is built from itself, so a unit always exists. Return the length of the shortest unit of s.

For example, "abcabcabc" has shortest unit "abc" (length 3); "aaaa" has length 1; "abaab" has no smaller unit than itself, so the answer is 5.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: The unit length must divide s.length. How many candidate lengths is that, and how can you test one?
A string of length n has period p if s[i] == s[i + p] for all valid i. The unit must also be a period, and the string must split evenly.
Compute the prefix function. The smallest period of the whole string is n - pi[n-1]; it is a unit length exactly when it divides n, otherwise the answer is n.
editorial: Testing every divisor d of n by comparing s with s[:d] repeated works and is fast enough here, but a single linear pass is possible.

Let b = pi[n-1] be the length of the longest proper border of s (a prefix that is also a suffix). Then s has smallest period p = n - b. If p divides n, the string is exactly n / p copies of its first p characters, and no shorter unit exists because any unit length is also a period and p is the smallest one.

If p does not divide n, the string only repeats its prefix a fractional number of times. Then any unit would have to be a period that divides n; one smaller than n would force the smallest period to divide n as well (a consequence of the periodicity lemma), which it does not. So the answer is n. Time O(n), space O(n).
